route: O-1 (extraordinary ability in the arts, or extraordinary achievement in motion pictures or television)

permit.applies: A United States employer, a United States agent, or a foreign employer through a United States agent petitions USCIS on Form I-129; the performer then seeks the visa or admission.
permit.first: The approved petition, which needs a written advisory opinion from the consulting peer group, labor and/or management organization.

fees.what: Form I-129, petition for O nonimmigrant worker, 1 to 25 named beneficiaries (small employers and nonprofits pay half)
Asylum Program Fee, any I-129 petitioner (small employer USD 300; nonprofit none)
Premium processing, O-1 or O-2 petition (optional)

permit.union: Consultation is mandatory before an O-1 petition is approved: for motion picture or television work, with the appropriate union representing the performer's occupational peers and a management organization; for other arts, with a peer group, which may include a labor organization. The opinions are advisory.
permit.eligibility: Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that a person described as prominent is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field of arts.
permit.payNote: None: 8 CFR 214.2(o), read whole, sets no minimum or prevailing wage for the O-1; a high salary is one of the optional evidentiary criteria, and an agent's contract must state the wage offered.
permit.exemptNote: None for paid work: the State Department's FAM holds B status not appropriate for a professional entertainer 'regardless of the amount or source of compensation'.

sources.title: 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38), definition of United States (GovInfo, 2023 edition)
sources.said: The term "United States", except as otherwise specifically herein provided, when used in a geographical sense, means the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands of the United States, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(o) Aliens of extraordinary ability or achievement (read again 2026-11-04 through the eCFR's versioner API, this page drawing its text by script)
sources.said: An O-1 or O-2 petition may only be filed by a United States employer, a United States agent, or a foreign employer through a United States agent. … is mandatory before a petition for an O-1 or O-2 classification can be approved. … who will be working on a motion picture or television production, consultation shall be made with the appropriate union representing the alien's occupational peers and a management organization in the area of the alien's ability. … Consultation with a peer group in the area of the alien's ability (which may include a labor organization), or a person or persons with expertise in the area of the alien's ability, is required in an O-1 petition for an alien of extraordinary ability. … Consultations are advisory and are not binding on the Service. … Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that a person described as prominent is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field of arts. … shall be valid for a period of time determined by the Director to be necessary to accomplish the event or activity, not to exceed 3 years. … An extension of stay may be authorized in increments of up to 1 year for an O-1 or O-2 beneficiary to continue or complete the same event or activity

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 106.4 Premium processing service (read again 2026-11-04 through the eCFR's versioner API, this page drawing its text by script)
sources.said: Petition for classification of a nonimmigrant described in section 101(a)(15)(O)(i) or (ii) of the INA—$2,965. … Petition for classification of a nonimmigrant described in section 101(a)(15)(O)(i) or (ii) of the Act: 15 business days.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State, Foreign Affairs Manual, 9 FAM 402.2-5(G) Entertainers and Artists (CT:VISA-1730, 03-10-2023; page last changed CT:VISA-2193, 03-19-2026)
sources.said: a. (U) Except for the following cases, B visa status is not appropriate for a member of the entertainment profession (professional entertainer) who seeks to enter the United States temporarily to perform services. Instead, performers should be accorded another appropriate visa classification, which in most cases will be P, regardless of the amount or source of compensation, whether the services will involve public appearance(s), or whether the performance is for charity or a U.S. based ethnic society. ... b. (U) The term “member of the entertainment profession” includes not only performing artists such as stage and movie actors, musicians, singers, and dancers ... 9 FAM 402.2-5(G)(1) ... A professional entertainer may be classified B-1 if the entertainer: (1) Is coming to the United States to participate only in a cultural program sponsored by the sending country; (2) Will be performing before a nonpaying audience; and (3) All expenses, including per diem, will be paid by the member’s government. 9 FAM 402.2-5(G)(2) ... A professional entertainer may be classified B-1 if the entertainer is coming to the United States to participate in a competition for which there is no remuneration other than a prize (monetary or otherwise) and expenses.

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(o) (as of 2026-10-30), read whole
sources.said: (o)(3)(iii) ... (8) Evidence that the alien has either commanded a high salary or will command a high salary or other remuneration for services, evidenced by contracts or other reliable evidence. (C) If the criteria in paragraph (o)(3)(iii) of this section do not readily apply to the beneficiary's occupation, the petitioner may submit comparable evidence ... [(o)(2)(iv)(E)(2)] An agent performing the function of an employer must provide the contractual agreement between the agent and the beneficiary which specifies the wage offered and the other terms and conditions of employment of the beneficiary.

note: The US Virgin Islands are part of the United States under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38)), so a performer works there on the United States' O-1. The petition is valid for the time needed for the event or activity, at most three years, and the stay can be extended in increments of up to a year to continue or complete it. The fee section carries a cross-reference to an amendment published at 91 FR 61984 (30 September 2026), not read (federalregister.gov and ecfr.gov now bot-check this client), so the fees may since have changed. The consular visa fee isn't included: travel.state.gov blocks this client. The eCFR copies cited were captured by curl in this environment at 06:20 on 2026-11-01 (files US-ecfr*.html); a later fetch was refused with a bot check. Read 2026-11-04, the US Virgin Islands taking the federal rules: the eCFR's 8 CFR 214.2 and the FAM (9 FAM 402.2). USCIS's processing time stays unknown (403).
